name: icx-mcp
title: Calera Infinite Context (ICX) — Persistent Memory
description: Persistent long-term memory and sub-5ms associative recall for AI agents and LLMs with zero context window decay.

tools.name: icx_remember
tools.description: Stores text documents, code snippets, architectural decisions, and factual knowledge into persistent long-term memory partitioned by space_id. Use this tool when saving important facts, project conventions, API keys, user preferences, or documentation for future sessions. Do NOT use for retrieving stored memory (use icx_recall_scoped for semantic QA, icx_search_facts for keyword lookup, or icx_quote_slot for verbatim quotes). Ingestion is additive and non-destructive: creates new memory nodes without overwriting or mutating existing records. Requires X-License-Key authentication.

text.description: The raw text, markdown document, code file, or factual statement to memorize (max ~500KB per call).

space_id.description: Optional memory space partition (e.g. 'default', 'codebase_docs', 'contracts_v2', 'user_preferences'). Defaults to 'default'.

filename.description: Optional filename or document title provenance tag (e.g. 'architecture.md', 'master_agreement.pdf') to track document origin.

family.description: Optional document family grouping for deterministic verbatim register quoting (e.g. 'contract.indemnity', 'auth.tokens'). When set, allows verbatim retrieval via icx_quote_slot.

learned_facts.description: Count of new simplicial facts learned

active_nodes.description: Total active nodes in memory space

bytes_ingested.description: Raw bytes stored in verbatim register

tools.name: icx_recall_scoped
tools.description: Performs semantic search across persistent long-term memory to retrieve grounded facts, relevant citations, and source documents matching a natural language question. Use this tool when answering questions about previously saved project specifications, codebase decisions, user preferences, or documents. Do NOT use for saving new facts (use icx_remember), do NOT use for raw keyword lookup (use icx_search_facts), and do NOT use for exact character-for-character verbatim quotes (use icx_quote_slot). Read-only operation with zero side effects. Requires X-License-Key authentication.

query.description: Natural language question, concept, or search prompt to recall relevant facts for.

space_id.description: Optional memory space partition to restrict recall to (e.g. 'default', 'codebase_docs'). Defaults to caller default space.

top_k.description: Maximum number of grounded facts to retrieve (default: 10, min: 1, max: 50).

facts.description: List of recalled grounded facts and citations

total_in_space.description: Total nodes in active memory space

tools.name: icx_search_facts
tools.description: Performs keyword and token search across persistent memory to discover entities, names, and matching terms within a memory space. Use this tool for entity exploration, keyword discovery, and locating specific identifiers or variables in memory. Do NOT use for answering natural language questions (use icx_recall_scoped), and do NOT use for writing data (use icx_remember). Read-only operation with zero side effects. Requires X-License-Key authentication.

query.description: Search keywords, entity names, or token substrings to look up across memory nodes.

space_id.description: Optional memory space partition to search within. Defaults to caller default space.

limit.description: Maximum number of node matches to return (default: 20, min: 1, max: 100).

matches.description: Simplicial complex nodes matching search query

total_in_space.description: Total nodes in active memory space

tools.name: icx_quote_slot
tools.description: Retrieves exact character-for-character verbatim text and cryptographic SHA-256 hashes from document registers by document family and 1-based slot index without AI paraphrasing. Use this tool when exact contractual wording, statutory clauses, license keys, or immutable code revisions must be quoted verbatim without AI modification. Do NOT use for semantic question answering (use icx_recall_scoped), and do NOT use for keyword exploration (use icx_search_facts). Read-only operation with zero side effects. Requires X-License-Key authentication.

family.description: Document family identifier specified during ingestion (e.g. 'contract.indemnity', 'msa.pricing', 'auth.tokens').

index.description: 1-based ordinal member index (e.g. 1 for first revision, 2 for second revision). Minimum: 1.

space_id.description: Optional memory space partition where the family was stored. Defaults to caller default space.

exact_quote.description: Verbatim character-exact text stored in register

tools.name: icx_inspect_space
tools.description: Audits and returns real-time diagnostic telemetry for a partitioned memory space, including active node counts, total synapses, grounded facts, memory state, and contradiction alarms. Use this tool to monitor memory partition health, verify document ingestion, check storage capacity, or detect contradiction alarms in a space. Do NOT use for querying memory content (use icx_recall_scoped or icx_quote_slot). Read-only operation with zero side effects. Requires X-License-Key authentication.

space_id.description: Optional memory space partition to inspect. Defaults to caller default space ('default').

tools.name: icx_reset_session
tools.description: Clears conversational dialogue turn history for a session while strictly preserving all underlying persistent memory, learned facts, and document registers in the memory space. Use this tool when switching conversation topics or clearing dialogue context between independent tasks while retaining stored knowledge. Do NOT use for wiping persistent memory (persistent memory is preserved by design). Mutates session turn state but leaves long-term memory intact. Requires X-License-Key authentication.

space_id.description: Optional memory space partition whose ephemeral session dialogue history should be reset. Defaults to caller default space.

memory_crystallized_preserved.description: Strictly true - underlying lattice memory is preserved
